materials.name: Ape Hide
materials.desc: Coarse black-brown fur on tough skin. Makes warm, rough-wearing jerkins and rugs.

materials.name: Ape Arm Sinew
materials.desc: Thick, springy tendons from the forearm that snap back like a drawn bowstring. Used for climbing gear and strength tonics.

materials.name: Ape Meat
materials.desc: Dark, lean and gamey flesh. Filling, if you can get past the resemblance.

materials.name: Axe Beak Beak
materials.desc: A wedge of dense, keratin-sheathed bone with a natural chopping edge. Hafted whole, it makes a brutal primitive axe.

materials.name: Axe Beak Feathers
materials.desc: Stiff, drab plumes too heavy for flight. Good fletching for heavy arrows and a cheap stuffing.

materials.name: Axe Beak Leg Sinew
materials.desc: Long, elastic tendons from a bird built to sprint. Runners' charms and swift-boot makers want them.

materials.name: Axe Beak Drumstick
materials.desc: A massive, fatty leg roast. One bird feeds a camp for two days.

materials.name: Baboon Pelt
materials.desc: Olive-grey fur with a coarse mane. Mostly used for trim and cheap caps.

materials.name: Baboon Fangs
materials.desc: Long, curved canines out of all proportion to the animal. Tribal charms for sly wits.

materials.name: Badger Hair
materials.desc: Stiff, silver-tipped guard hairs that hold water and pigment. The best brushes for painters and scribes.

materials.name: Badger Claws
materials.desc: Short, spade-like claws worn smooth from digging. Miners carry them for luck; artificers use them in digging charms.

materials.name: Bat Wing
materials.desc: Paper-thin, veined membrane that crackles faintly when stretched. A classic reagent for echo-sense and night-flight draughts.

materials.name: Bat Ear
materials.desc: A wrinkled, oversized ear still tuned to impossibly high tones. Hedge wizards grind them into hearing tinctures.

materials.name: Black Bear Pelt
materials.desc: Glossy black fur, dense and oily enough to shrug off rain. A trapper's winter coat.

materials.name: Black Bear Claws
materials.desc: Curved, dark claws built to hook bark. Used in climbing spikes and woodsman's charms.

materials.name: Black Bear Fat
materials.desc: Rendered into a white, sweet-smelling grease for lamps, leather and chapped hands.

materials.name: Black Bear Meat
materials.desc: Rich, dark, and heavy. Must be cooked through; bears carry worms.

materials.name: Blood Hawk Plume
materials.desc: A rust-red flight feather with a darker vein, like a dried bloodstain. Prized for fletching and flight charms.

materials.name: Blood Hawk Talons
materials.desc: Needle-sharp hooked talons. Hunters wear them to sharpen the eye for a kill.

materials.name: Boar Tusks
materials.desc: Curved ivory tusks, yellowed and razor-edged. A classic talisman of stubborn endurance.

materials.name: Boar Hide
materials.desc: Thick, bristly skin that tans into hard, scuffed leather for boots and bracers.

materials.name: Boar Meat
materials.desc: Sweet, fatty pork, far better than any farm pig.

materials.name: Brown Bear Pelt
materials.desc: A vast, heavy pelt of brown fur. Sleeping under one is like sleeping beside a banked hearth.

materials.name: Brown Bear Claws
materials.desc: Blunt, finger-long claws that could rake stone. The warrior's first trophy in many clans.

materials.name: Brown Bear Fat
materials.desc: Pounds of pale fat, rendered for lamp oil, waterproofing and salves.

materials.name: Brown Bear Meat
materials.desc: Enough rich, dark meat for a village feast. Cook it well.

materials.name: Camel Hide
materials.desc: Thin, tough, sand-coloured leather favoured for waterskins and saddlebags.

materials.name: Camel Hump Fat
materials.desc: Dense, waxy fat that keeps for weeks. Desert cooks render it into a trail staple that wards off thirst and fatigue.

materials.name: Camel Hair
materials.desc: Soft underfleece that spins into warm, fine yarn for desert cloaks.

materials.name: Cat Whiskers
materials.desc: Stiff, translucent whiskers that twitch at the faintest draught. Thieves sew them into gloves for a quiet touch.

materials.name: Constrictor Snake Skin
materials.desc: Patterned, glossy skin that stretches and grips. Wrapped around hilts and bow grips it never slips.

materials.name: Constrictor Coil Muscle
materials.desc: Bands of flat, fibrous muscle that still clench when cut. Dried into cords of unnatural holding strength.

materials.name: Constrictor Snake Meat
materials.desc: White, chicken-like flesh in long ropes.

materials.name: Crab Shell
materials.desc: A small, mottled shell. Crushed into grit for polishing or glazes; charm-makers use it for small wards.

materials.name: Crab Meat
materials.desc: Sweet flesh from claws and body. A mouthful, but a good one.

materials.name: Crocodile Hide
materials.desc: Ridged, armoured skin with bony plates in the back. Tanned, it makes stiff, dagger-proof leather.

materials.name: Crocodile Teeth
materials.desc: Conical teeth that are constantly shed and regrown. Common in swamp-folk charms of grip and hold.

materials.name: Crocodile Meat
materials.desc: Pale tail meat, somewhere between fish and fowl.

materials.name: Deer Hide
materials.desc: Soft, supple hide that tans into buckskin for gloves, shirts and pouches.

materials.name: Deer Antler
materials.desc: Branched, bone-hard antler. Carved into knife handles, toggles and tool grips.

materials.name: Venison
materials.desc: Lean, dark, famously good meat.

materials.name: Dire Wolf Pelt
materials.desc: The silent grey fur of the deep-forest hunter: thick, smoke-coloured and strangely hushed against branches. Rangers' cloaks of choice.

materials.name: Dire Wolf Fang
materials.desc: A thumb-long canine, yellowed and wickedly sharp. Worn as a pack-hunter's token.

materials.name: Dire Wolf Snout
materials.desc: The wet nasal organ of a beast that tracks by scent across miles. Alchemists steep it into tracker's tinctures.

materials.name: Dire Wolf Meat
materials.desc: Stringy and strong-tasting, but plentiful in a hard winter.

materials.name: Draft Horse Hide
materials.desc: Heavy, broad hide that tans into thick harness leather.

materials.name: Draft Horse Hooves
materials.desc: Big, dense hooves, boiled down into strong hide glue.

materials.name: Draft Horse Sinew
materials.desc: Great ropes of tendon from a beast bred to pull. Backing for heavy bows and hauling tackle.

materials.name: Eagle Eye
materials.desc: A golden, glassy eye that seems to focus even in death. Key ingredient in far-sight potions and scout's lenses.

materials.name: Eagle Feathers
materials.desc: Broad, barred flight feathers. Excellent fletching and a staple of flight charms.

materials.name: Elephant Ivory Tusk
materials.desc: A curving, cream-white tusk as long as a man. Carved into hilts, holy symbols and strength talismans.

materials.name: Elephant Hide
materials.desc: Deeply wrinkled grey hide a finger thick. Tanned, it makes heavy, near-impenetrable shields and hide armour.

materials.name: Elephant Heart
materials.desc: A heart the size of a barrel, still slow and heavy. Said to lend a giant's endurance to brews.

materials.name: Elephant Bone
materials.desc: Huge, heavy long-bones for tent poles, tool handles and carving.

materials.name: Elephant Meat
materials.desc: Tough, coarse and endless. Feeds a whole caravan.

materials.name: Elk Antler
materials.desc: A broad, palmate antler rack. Carvers make bows, pick-handles and battle charms from it.

materials.name: Elk Hide
materials.desc: Thick, soft hide good for moccasins and winter tents.

materials.name: Elk Meat
materials.desc: Rich red meat, a winter's larder in one animal.

materials.name: Flying Snake Venom Sac
materials.desc: A tiny sac of burning venom. Potent for its size; poisoners distil it into fast blade toxins.

materials.name: Flying Snake Feathers
materials.desc: Iridescent green and gold feathers from the serpent's wings. Beautiful fletching and a light flight reagent.

materials.name: Frog Skin
materials.desc: A slick, mottled skin that stays damp far longer than it should. Swimmers' charms and hedge potions use it.

materials.name: Frog Legs
materials.desc: A delicate, pale morsel. Fried, they're a delicacy in marsh towns.

materials.name: Giant Ape Hide
materials.desc: A vast, dark pelt on skin thick as saddle leather. Enough for a dozen heavy cloaks or a chieftain's tent.

materials.name: Giant Ape Heart
materials.desc: A thundering heart as big as a cask. The keystone of brews that grant towering, bestial strength.

materials.name: Giant Ape Arm Sinew
materials.desc: Cable-thick tendons that can hold a wagon aloft. Used for siege bowstrings and gauntlets of might.

materials.name: Giant Ape Skull
materials.desc: A heavy-browed skull big enough to wear as a helm. Barbarian warlords mount them as war trophies.

materials.name: Giant Ape Meat
materials.desc: Mountains of dark, gamey meat.

materials.name: Giant Badger Pelt
materials.desc: Grizzled grey fur with a bold striped face. Rough, warm and hard-wearing.

materials.name: Giant Badger Claws
materials.desc: Heavy, shovel-shaped claws caked with packed soil. Miners and sappers use them in digging charms and tools.

materials.name: Giant Badger Musk Gland
materials.desc: A reeking scent gland. Trappers smear it on snares to lure or ward off burrowers.

materials.name: Giant Bat Wing Membrane
materials.desc: A sail of leathery, veined skin, light and strong. Used for gliders, flight charms and cave-sense cloaks.

materials.name: Giant Bat Ear
materials.desc: A folded ear the size of a hand, attuned to sounds no person hears. Distilled into echo-sight reagents.

materials.name: Giant Bat Fangs
materials.desc: Small, needle-thin fangs useful as awls or arrow tips.

materials.name: Giant Boar Tusks
materials.desc: Huge, curling tusks scarred from a hundred fights. Relentless warriors wear them as proof of grit.

materials.name: Giant Boar Hide
materials.desc: Bristle-covered hide a thumb thick. Tans into scarred, sturdy leather for armour.

materials.name: Giant Boar Heart
materials.desc: A heart that keeps thumping for a minute after death. Tonics of it help a warrior stay standing after a killing blow.

materials.name: Giant Boar Meat
materials.desc: Mountains of rich, fatty pork. A lord's feast.

materials.name: Giant Centipede Venom Gland
materials.desc: A pair of amber glands behind the fangs. The venom numbs flesh and can lock the limbs of a weakened victim.

materials.name: Giant Centipede Carapace Plates
materials.desc: Glossy, segmented plates with little hooked leg-stubs. Stitched to gloves and boots for grip on stone.

materials.name: Giant Constrictor Skin
materials.desc: A great patterned hide of overlapping scales, supple and nearly tearproof. Used for grapnel-grip gloves and wrestling harnesses.

materials.name: Giant Constrictor Coil Muscle
materials.desc: Thick bands of muscle that clench even after death. Dried and braided, they make ropes and bindings that simply won't let go.

materials.name: Giant Constrictor Fangs
materials.desc: Backward-curving, non-venomous fangs, good for fishhooks and awls.

materials.name: Giant Constrictor Meat
materials.desc: Yards of pale, mild meat.

materials.name: Giant Crab Shell
materials.desc: Mottled carapace plates as tough as boiled leather; the domed back plate alone makes a buckler, and coast folk lace the rest into shields.

materials.name: Giant Crab Pincer
materials.desc: A heavy claw that still clamps if you press the right tendon. Used in clamps, grapples and holding charms.

materials.name: Giant Crab Meat
materials.desc: Sweet white claw-meat, plenty for a shore feast.

materials.name: Giant Crocodile Hide
materials.desc: Ridged, bony armour plates set in leather thick as a board. Makes superb, heavy scale armour.

materials.name: Giant Crocodile Teeth
materials.desc: Teeth like spearheads, conical and heavy. Crushing-grip charms and fearsome arrowheads.

materials.name: Giant Crocodile Tail Sinew
materials.desc: Massive tendons from the tail that drove the beast through water. Used for swimming charms and heavy crossbow strings.

materials.name: Giant Crocodile Heart
materials.desc: A slow, cold heart that can idle for an hour underwater. The base of breath-holding draughts.

materials.name: Giant Crocodile Meat
materials.desc: Pale, heavy tail meat, a swamp village's feast.

materials.name: Giant Eagle Pinion Feather
materials.desc: A golden-brown flight feather as long as an arm. The finest fletching known, and a core flight reagent.

materials.name: Giant Eagle Eye
materials.desc: A huge amber eye with astonishing clarity. Distilled into far-sight elixirs and scouts' lenses.

materials.name: Giant Eagle Talons
materials.desc: Hooked talons as long as daggers, built to lift a horse. Mountain clans mount them as knife hilts.

materials.name: Giant Elk Antler Rack
materials.desc: A vast crown of antler spanning twice a man's height. Carved into bows, staves and druidic totems.

materials.name: Giant Elk Hide
materials.desc: A huge, soft, fawn-brown hide. Enough for a lodge's walls.

materials.name: Giant Elk Heart
materials.desc: A great heart that drove the elk across miles of forest. Tonics of it quicken the runner's stride.

materials.name: Giant Elk Meat
materials.desc: Enough lean venison to keep a village through a winter month.

materials.name: Giant Fire Beetle Gland
materials.desc: A pulpy, orange-glowing gland. Removed intact, it keeps shedding warm light for 1d6 days — a smokeless lantern for miners.

materials.name: Giant Fire Beetle Carapace
materials.desc: A glossy red-black shell. Makes bowls, buckler faces and decorative inlay.

materials.name: Giant Frog Tongue
materials.desc: A long, sticky, elastic tongue. Dried, it makes a gluey lash used for grapnels and snares.

materials.name: Giant Frog Skin
materials.desc: A slick, mottled skin that sheds water and never quite dries. A key ingredient in swimming salves.

materials.name: Giant Frog Legs
materials.desc: Two huge hind legs of pale, tender meat. A marsh delicacy.

materials.name: Giant Goat Horns
materials.desc: Thick, ridged, back-swept horns. Carved into climbing picks, drinking horns and rams' charms.

materials.name: Giant Goat Hooves
materials.desc: Split, rubbery-soled hooves that grip the barest ledge. Cobblers set them in climbing boots.

materials.name: Giant Goat Fleece
materials.desc: A shaggy, cream-coloured coat that keeps out mountain cold.

materials.name: Giant Goat Meat
materials.desc: Tough, strong-flavoured mutton.

materials.name: Giant Hyena Pelt
materials.desc: Coarse, spotted fur that always smells faintly of carrion.

materials.name: Giant Hyena Jaw
materials.desc: A massive jaw with crushing molars that can crack a thighbone. Mounted as a bone-breaker's trophy.

materials.name: Giant Hyena Larynx
materials.desc: The voice box behind that awful laughter. Tricksters and bards use it for mocking-voice charms.

materials.name: Giant Lizard Hide
materials.desc: Pebbled, tough hide that tans into good scaled leather.

materials.name: Giant Lizard Toe Pads
materials.desc: Ridged, grippy pads from the feet. Glued to gloves and boots for sure footing on sheer rock.

materials.name: Giant Lizard Meat
materials.desc: Chewy white meat, a staple of Underdark travellers.

materials.name: Giant Octopus Ink Sac
materials.desc: A black, rubbery sac full of dense ink. Scribes value it; alchemists make smoke-and-shadow concoctions from it.

materials.name: Giant Octopus Tentacle
materials.desc: A long, suckered arm that still clings to anything it touches. Grapnel pads and swimming charms.

materials.name: Giant Octopus Skin
materials.desc: Shimmering skin that shifts colour for hours after death. Tailors of camouflage cloaks pay well for it.

materials.name: Giant Octopus Beak
materials.desc: A hard, parrot-like black beak. Carved into scrapers and amulets.

materials.name: Giant Owl Feathers
materials.desc: Downy-edged flight feathers that make no sound in the air. Prized for silent fletching and hushed cloaks.

materials.name: Giant Owl Eyes
materials.desc: Huge, golden eyes that gather the faintest light. The base of night-sight draughts.

materials.name: Giant Owl Talons
materials.desc: Hooked, grey talons. Hunters' trophies and hooks.

materials.name: Giant Poisonous Snake Venom Sac
materials.desc: A pair of amber sacs, heavy with venom. The most common source of serpent poison for blades.

materials.name: Giant Poisonous Snake Fangs
materials.desc: Hollow, hinged fangs. Poisoners set them in rings and needle traps.

materials.name: Giant Poisonous Snake Skin
materials.desc: Diamond-patterned scaled skin, pretty for belts and scabbards.

materials.name: Giant Rat Pelt
materials.desc: Greasy grey-brown fur. Cheap lining for poor folk's coats — best boiled first.

materials.name: Giant Rat Incisors
materials.desc: Long, orange, chisel-shaped teeth that never stop growing. Used as tiny gouges and thieves' good-luck tokens.

materials.name: Diseased Rat Blood
materials.desc: Dark, clotted blood thick with sickness. Plague doctors study it; poisoners and cultists want it for darker reasons.

materials.name: Giant Scorpion Stinger
materials.desc: A curved, bulb-tipped stinger still full of burning venom. Poisoners milk it; weaponsmiths set the barb in spear tips.

materials.name: Giant Scorpion Carapace
materials.desc: Sand-coloured, overlapping plates harder than cured bronze. Fitted into light, tough armour.

materials.name: Giant Scorpion Pincers
materials.desc: Two heavy, serrated claws. Used for clamps, trophies and gripping-gauntlet charms.

materials.name: Giant Scorpion Meat
materials.desc: Pale, shellfish-like meat from the tail and legs. Nomads roast it in the shell.

materials.name: Giant Sea Horse Swim Bladder
materials.desc: A translucent, air-filled bladder. Alchemists make water-breathing and buoyancy draughts from it.

materials.name: Giant Sea Horse Dorsal Fin
materials.desc: A fan-like, rippling fin that drove the beast through currents. Sewn onto swimming gear for speed.

materials.name: Giant Sea Horse Hide
materials.desc: Ridged, bony hide in pastel colours; makes a flexible, pretty leather.

materials.name: Giant Shark Teeth
materials.desc: Serrated, palm-sized teeth in endless rows. Used as blade edges, arrowheads and sea-raider charms.

materials.name: Giant Shark Skin
materials.desc: Rough, sandpaper-like skin that glides one way and rasps the other. Makes grip wraps, shagreen and swimmer's leather.

materials.name: Giant Shark Liver Oil
materials.desc: Barrels of thick, pale oil from an enormous liver. Used for lamps, waterproofing and buoyancy salves.

materials.name: Giant Shark Snout
materials.desc: The pitted snout that sensed blood and heartbeats from afar. Distilled into tinctures of uncanny perception.

materials.name: Giant Shark Meat
materials.desc: Coarse, strong meat that must be soaked before eating.

materials.name: Giant Spider Silk
materials.desc: Sticky, strong strands pulled from the spinnerets. Spun into rope, climbing lines and fine thread.

materials.name: Giant Spider Venom Gland
materials.desc: A paired gland of pale, thick venom. A favourite base for poisoners.

materials.name: Giant Spider Eye Cluster
materials.desc: A mass of black, glittering eyes. Ground into draughts of keen perception and dark-sight.

materials.name: Giant Spider Carapace
materials.desc: A glossy, bristled black shell. Used for bowls, masks and inlay.

materials.name: Giant Toad Poison Gland
materials.desc: A warty gland oozing milky toxin. Poisoners and hallucinogen-brewers both want it.

materials.name: Giant Toad Tongue
materials.desc: A thick, sticky tongue that can pull a grown man. Dried into sticky lashes and grapples.

materials.name: Giant Toad Skin
materials.desc: Bumpy, damp skin that repels water. Swimming salves and marsh boots.

materials.name: Giant Toad Legs
materials.desc: Thick, pale legs, edible once the skin is off.

materials.name: Giant Vulture Feathers
materials.desc: Dark, broad flight feathers built for endless soaring. Cheaper flight reagents and fletching.

materials.name: Giant Vulture Stomach
materials.desc: A tough, acid-soaked stomach that digests rot without harm. A key reagent in antidotes and anti-plague tonics.

materials.name: Giant Vulture Eyes
materials.desc: Pale, sharp eyes that spot a corpse from a mile up. Used in far-sight draughts.

materials.name: Giant Wasp Stinger
materials.desc: A glossy barbed stinger backed by a sac of burning venom. Poisoners milk it; hunters tip darts with it.

materials.name: Giant Wasp Wings
materials.desc: Clear, veined wings that still hum faintly when flicked. A core reagent in swift-flight charms.

materials.name: Giant Wasp Carapace
materials.desc: Striped yellow-black chitin, light and glossy. Decorative inlay and toys.

materials.name: Giant Weasel Pelt
materials.desc: Sleek, glossy fur, white in winter and brown in summer. Nobles and thieves both wear it for its silent softness.

materials.name: Giant Weasel Scent Gland
materials.desc: A small, pungent musk gland. Trackers use it to train hunting dogs.

materials.name: Giant Weasel Fangs
materials.desc: Small, sharp fangs; a hunter's token.

materials.name: Giant Wolf Spider Venom Gland
materials.desc: A small gland of fast-acting venom. Poisoners call it a working-man's poison.

materials.name: Giant Wolf Spider Eyes
materials.desc: Eight glittering eyes that shine in torchlight. Ground into night-sight reagents.

materials.name: Giant Wolf Spider Leg Bristles
materials.desc: Stiff, sensitive hairs that felt the smallest tremor and let the spider run up walls. Sewn into climbing gloves.

materials.name: Goat Horn
materials.desc: Ridged, curving horn. Carved into drinking horns, buttons and climber's charms.

materials.name: Goat Hide
materials.desc: A thin, tough hide; goatskin is the scribe's favourite source for vellum.

materials.name: Goat Meat
materials.desc: Lean, strong-tasting meat, a staple of hill folk.

materials.name: Giant Spider Silk Rope
materials.desc: A slender, pale rope twisted from cleaned spider silk. Lighter and stronger than hemp and barely sticky to the touch.

recipe.lore: Oiling the raw strands strips the stickiness while keeping their spring and strength.

materials.name: Spider Silk Thread
materials.desc: Fine, shimmering thread spun from giant spider silk. Tailors of magic garments prize it for seams that never part.

recipe.lore: Washed in an alchemical rinse and spun fine, the silk keeps its binding strength in a thread thin enough for embroidery.

materials.name: Octopus Ink
materials.desc: A deep, smoky black ink that seems to swallow light. Scribes use it for scrolls of concealment and darkness.

recipe.lore: Strained and thickened, the octopus's escape-cloud becomes an ink suited to scrolls of hiding.

monsters.name: Ape
monsters.blurb: A shaggy, powerful climber of jungle canopies and wooded crags; its long arms are all corded muscle.

harvest.note: Cut along the full length of the arm; tendons severed short are only good for glue.

monsters.name: Axe Beak
monsters.blurb: A tall, flightless bird that runs down prey and splits it with a hatchet-shaped beak.

harvest.note: Pry it off at the skull seam; a hacked-off beak cracks along its length.

monsters.name: Baboon
monsters.blurb: A loud, clever troop primate with shocking fangs and a knack for ganging up.

monsters.name: Badger
monsters.blurb: A stubborn, bad-tempered digger with a striped face and a nose that finds anything underground.

harvest.note: Pluck only the back guard hairs; the belly fur is worthless.

monsters.name: Bat
monsters.blurb: A tiny night flier that sees with sound.

harvest.note: Dry it spread on a frame, or it curls into a useless scab.

monsters.name: Black Bear
monsters.blurb: A sturdy, omnivorous bear that climbs well and raids camps for honey and salt pork.

harvest.note: Late-autumn pelts are thickest; a summer kill is worth half.

monsters.name: Blood Hawk
monsters.blurb: A crimson-feathered raptor that hunts in shrieking flocks and goes wild at the smell of blood.

monsters.name: Boar
monsters.blurb: A bristling wild pig that charges first and keeps fighting past the point it should drop.

monsters.name: Brown Bear
monsters.blurb: A towering, hump-shouldered bear whose paws can break a horse's back.

harvest.note: Needs two people and an hour to lift and skin without tearing.

monsters.name: Camel
monsters.blurb: A patient, foul-tempered desert beast that walks for days without water.

harvest.note: Comb, don't cut; the long guard hairs ruin the yarn.

monsters.name: Cat
monsters.blurb: A small, silent hunter of mice and alleys.

harvest.note: Only the long upper whiskers count — and many cat-owners will consider you a monster.

monsters.name: Constrictor Snake
monsters.blurb: A thick-bodied snake that kills by coiling and squeezing.

harvest.note: Peel it from the head in one tube; slit skins lose half their value.

monsters.name: Crab
monsters.blurb: A sideways-scuttling shoreline crab.

monsters.name: Crocodile
monsters.blurb: A log-shaped ambusher that drags prey under and holds it there.

harvest.note: Only the belly skin tans soft; keep the back plates for studded armour.

monsters.name: Deer
monsters.blurb: A skittish grazer, and the most common quarry of any hunter.

harvest.note: Only bucks carry antlers, and only outside of spring.

monsters.name: Dire Wolf
monsters.blurb: A horse-sized wolf that hunts in silent packs through deep, snowbound forests.

harvest.note: Must be skinned in one piece or the cloak-grade value is lost.
Must be packed in salt within the hour or its sense-lore fades.

monsters.name: Draft Horse
monsters.blurb: A broad, patient workhorse bred to haul ploughs and wagons.

harvest.note: Tail and mane hair, cut without harm to a living animal too.

monsters.name: Eagle
monsters.blurb: A keen-eyed raptor that stoops from great heights.

harvest.note: Remove with a spoon, never a blade; a punctured eye is ruined.

monsters.name: Elephant
monsters.blurb: A colossal grey herd-beast that tramples anything threatening its young.

harvest.note: Must be sawn at the root with care; a cracked tusk loses most of its worth.
Takes a team and a full day to strip.

monsters.name: Elk
monsters.blurb: A tall deer of the north woods, crowned with a great rack.

harvest.note: Bulls shed antlers in late winter; a kill then may leave you with nothing.

monsters.name: Flying Snake
monsters.blurb: A brightly feathered little serpent that glides through jungle air. Wizards keep them as messengers.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.

monsters.name: Frog
monsters.blurb: A small pond frog.

monsters.name: Giant Ape
monsters.blurb: A mountainous ape that hurls boulders and tears trees apart when angered.

harvest.note: Requires hours of work and several hands; flaying under a hot sun spoils it.
Must be drained and packed in salt within the hour.

monsters.name: Giant Badger
monsters.blurb: A dog-sized badger that can dig through packed earth as fast as a man walks.

harvest.note: Burst it (fail by 5+) and you stink for a day, with disadvantage on Stealth against creatures that smell.

monsters.name: Giant Bat
monsters.blurb: A bat with a wingspan wider than a wagon, hunting by echo in deep caves.

harvest.note: Stretch and dry within a day or it shrinks and tears.

monsters.name: Giant Boar
monsters.blurb: A pony-sized boar with sword-length tusks that keeps charging long after it ought to fall.

harvest.note: Must be taken while it still beats, within minutes of the kill.

monsters.name: Giant Centipede
monsters.blurb: A long, many-legged horror whose bite leaves victims numb and limp.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.

monsters.name: Giant Constrictor Snake
monsters.blurb: A serpent long enough to coil around a rowboat and crush it.

harvest.note: Peel in one tube from the head; takes several people and two hours.

monsters.name: Giant Crab
monsters.blurb: A dog-sized crab that lurks in surf and grapples with oversized claws.

harvest.note: Crack it at the rear seam; a split front shell is scrap.

monsters.name: Giant Crocodile
monsters.blurb: A crocodile long as a longship, able to drag a horse beneath the black water.

harvest.note: The back plates must be flayed intact; takes most of a day.
Must be sealed in brine within the hour.

monsters.name: Giant Eagle
monsters.blurb: A noble, speaking eagle of the high peaks; most good folk see harvesting one as a crime, but fallen ones are still found.

harvest.note: Among many elves and dwarves, owning one taken from a murdered eagle is a grave insult.
Remove gently within the hour; the lens clouds quickly.

monsters.name: Giant Elk
monsters.blurb: A majestic elk tall as a house, revered by druids and rarely seen by others.

harvest.note: Druids and forest folk may take grave offence at a harvest from their sacred beast.

monsters.name: Giant Fire Beetle
monsters.blurb: A dog-sized beetle whose glands shed a steady orange glow.

harvest.note: Handle gently; a squashed gland goes dark at once. The glow lasts 1d6 days after harvest.

monsters.name: Giant Frog
monsters.blurb: A frog big enough to swallow a halfling whole, snaring prey with its tongue.

harvest.note: Keep it wet until it's stretched on a frame to dry; left crumpled, it dries brittle within the hour.

monsters.name: Giant Goat
monsters.blurb: An ox-sized mountain goat that bounds up cliffs and rams intruders off ledges.

monsters.name: Giant Hyena
monsters.blurb: A cackling, bone-crunching scavenger that follows armies and plagues.

monsters.name: Giant Lizard
monsters.blurb: A horse-sized lizard used as a mount and pack beast in the deep places.

monsters.name: Giant Octopus
monsters.blurb: A reef-dwelling octopus with arms longer than a boat, masking its escapes in clouds of ink.

harvest.note: Pierce it (fail by 5+) and it spills, blinding you until you wash your eyes.
Keep it in seawater; out of water, the colour-cells die within the day.

monsters.name: Giant Owl
monsters.blurb: A wise, silent forest owl that sometimes befriends elves and druids.

harvest.note: Harvest before dawn; sunlight clouds them within minutes.

monsters.name: Giant Poisonous Snake
monsters.blurb: A man-length viper with fangs that deliver a killing dose.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.

monsters.name: Giant Rat
monsters.blurb: A dog-sized sewer rat that swarms in packs and bites anything that moves.

monsters.name: Giant Rat (Diseased)
monsters.blurb: A mangy, weeping giant rat whose bite carries sickness.

harvest.note: Boil before use; a raw diseased pelt can pass on the sickness.
Failing by 5+ exposes you to the rat's disease.

monsters.name: Giant Scorpion
monsters.blurb: A cart-sized scorpion that seizes prey in its claws and stings it to death.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.
Separate the plates at their joints; hacked plates are only good as scrap.
Cut the venom gland away first or the meat is toxic.

monsters.name: Giant Sea Horse
monsters.blurb: A graceful, horse-sized sea horse ridden by merfolk and sea elves.

harvest.note: Punctured bladders are useless; lift it out whole.

monsters.name: Giant Shark
monsters.blurb: A shark as long as a warship that smells blood through miles of sea.

harvest.note: Skinning must be done against the grain or the skin shreds.
Render the liver within a day; a Huge shark gives barrels, but only the clear first skimming is reagent-grade.
Packed in salt within the hour or its sense-lore fades.

monsters.name: Giant Spider
monsters.blurb: A horse-sized spider that spins webs across whole clearings and feels every tremor in them.

harvest.note: Draw the silk from the spinnerets while still warm; old webbing is filthy and weak.
Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.
Harvest within the hour; the eyes weep and cloud quickly.

monsters.name: Giant Toad
monsters.blurb: A pony-sized toad with a poisonous bite that swallows victims whole.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.
Must be skinned carefully; any toxin on the meat causes vomiting.

monsters.name: Giant Vulture
monsters.blurb: A bald, huge-winged carrion bird that circles over battlefields and dying travellers.

harvest.note: The acid burns; failing by 5+ deals 1d4 acid damage.

monsters.name: Giant Wasp
monsters.blurb: A dog-sized wasp whose sting is dripping with venom.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.
Brittle; pack flat between cloth or they shatter.

monsters.name: Giant Weasel
monsters.blurb: A sleek, fast hunter with a white winter coat, the size of a hound.

harvest.note: Winter pelts (pure white) are worth double.

monsters.name: Giant Wolf Spider
monsters.blurb: A hairy, pony-sized hunting spider that runs down prey rather than webbing it.

harvest.note: Rupture the venom sac (fail by 5+) and you're exposed to its poison.
Harvest within the hour; they cloud quickly.

monsters.name: Goat
monsters.blurb: A sure-footed, stubborn domestic goat.
